parts.title: My first ballet class
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When I was ten, my parents sent me to a ballet class. I did not want to go. In my school, football was the only sport for boys, and I was afraid that my friends would laugh at me.

On the first day, I was the only boy in the room. The teacher, Madame Roux, was a tall woman with a kind voice. She showed us how to stand with our feet turned out, and told us to imagine a string pulling us up from the top of our heads. It was much harder than it looked. After one hour, my legs were shaking.

But something strange happened. After a few weeks, I began to enjoy it. Dancing made me feel strong and free, and I forgot about my worries. In the end, I told my friends. To my surprise, nobody laughed. One of them even asked if he could try it.

Now I am sixteen, and I dance for a youth company. Last month, I played the lead in a show, and my football friends came to watch. They stood up and clapped for a long time. That was the best moment of my life.

questions.explanation: He was afraid that his friends would laugh at him.

parts.title: A short history of ballet
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Ballet began more than five hundred years ago in the courts of Italy. [1] Rich families organised parties with music, food and dancing to show their power.

The art then moved to France, where King Louis the Fourteenth loved to dance. [2] He even performed himself, and he started the first school for dancers in the year sixteen sixty-one.

In the beginning, the dancers wore heavy costumes and shoes with heels. [3] This changed in the nineteenth century, when women began to dance on the tips of their toes in soft shoes.

The Russian dancers and teachers became famous around the world. [4] Some of the best-known ballets, such as Swan Lake, were written at that time and are still performed today.

Today, ballet is danced in almost every country. [5] Many young people take lessons, even if they never plan to become professional dancers.
sentences: The music for them was very quiet and sad.
The king believed that dance was important to the nation.
Ballet shoes were first made from soft leather.
This made the movements slow and difficult to follow.
It was a way to entertain guests at big dinners.
People were amazed by how light and graceful they looked.
Their ideas came from a book about dance written in Italy.
Companies have even been founded in cities which had no theatres before.

gaps.explanation: Entertaining guests at big dinners follows the beginnings in Italy and leads to parties with music.
The king believed that dance was important, and the next sentence says he performed himself.
Heavy costumes made the movements slow, and the next sentence says things changed.
People were amazed by the Russian dancers, and ballets of that time are still performed.
Companies founded in new cities fit with ballet being danced in almost every country.

parts.title: Why dance is good for you
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Dancing is not only fun, but it is also very good for your body and mind. When you dance, you move all your muscles, [1] makes you stronger and more flexible. It can also improve your memory, [2] you have to remember the steps and the music. Many people say that dancing helps them to feel happier, because it takes their mind off their worries. You do not have to be young [3] be good at it: there are classes for people of every age. If you are shy, you can start by dancing at home in front of the mirror. Little by little, you will become more confident, and one day, you may find [4] dancing in front of other people. If you prefer to dance [5] a group, many clubs are happy to welcome new members. All you need is a pair of comfortable shoes [6] the wish to try.

gaps.explanation: Which refers to moving all your muscles and acts as a relative pronoun.
It improves memory because you remember steps: reason.
Young to be good at it: too/enough structure with an infinitive.
Find yourself dancing means discover that you are doing it.
Dance in a group: the usual preposition for a group.
A pair of shoes and the wish to try: both things are needed.

parts.title: A talk about a dance school
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: marguerite
turns.text: Hello, and welcome to the Starlight Dance School. My name is Joyce, and I am the head teacher. Before we begin the tour, let me tell you a little about us. Our school started with just one small room above a bakery. People think it’s older than it is, because the building is so old, but we opened our doors twenty years ago. Some friends say it was only fifteen, but they forget the first year in the bakery. Today we have about three hundred students. I know, it sounds like a lot. Two years ago we had only two hundred, and next year I hope to reach four hundred, but we need to build another studio first. Our students come from every part of the city. The youngest is four, and she is very serious about it. Most children are between six and twelve. But dancing isn’t just for the young. Our oldest student is seventy, and she comes twice a week. Her husband is sixty-eight, and he started last year after he watched her. Let me tell you about the timetable. The advanced groups meet from Tuesday to Friday, but the beginners’ classes are on Mondays and Wednesdays. We used to have a Friday group for beginners, but nobody could come, so we stopped it. All classes begin at five and finish at six. Now, the price. A single lesson costs eight pounds. If you buy ten lessons together, it’s seventy pounds, which is seven pounds each, and a monthly card for unlimited classes is fifty. Most families find the lessons good value. The first lesson is free, so please try it. Finally, our big event. Every year we hold a show in the city theatre. It was in May when we started, then we moved to July for a few years because of the heat. Now it’s in June, always the second Saturday, and we hope that you will all come and watch. Tickets go on sale in March. Now, please follow me, and I will show you the studios.

gaps.explanation: The school opened twenty years ago; some friends say fifteen, but they forget the first year.

parts.title: An interview with a young dancer
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Josefa, you started dancing very young. Why did you begin?

turns.speaker: d
turns.text: People think my parents sent me, or that a teacher at school noticed me, but no. When I was five, my grandmother took me to see a ballet, and I couldn’t speak for the whole evening. I told her I would be on that stage one day. The next week, I joined my first class.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: How long do you practise every day?

turns.speaker: d
turns.text: It depends on the period of the year. When I was at school, I did about three hours after class, and only at weekends it was ten, because there were no lessons. Now it’s about six hours every day, three in the morning and three in the afternoon, with a short break for lunch. It sounds like a lot, and my friends say I’m crazy, but I love it, so it doesn’t feel like work to me.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What about pain?

turns.speaker: d
turns.text: People imagine I never feel pain, but my feet hurt every day. I don’t stop because of it, though. And on stage it’s strange: the lights come on and I forget about it completely. It’s afterwards, in the dressing room, when I take my shoes off, that I feel it again. My mother always says that I should see a doctor, and of course I do, twice a year, but a dancer has to accept a little pain as part of the job.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do you eat before a show?

turns.speaker: d
turns.text: Some dancers eat nothing, only water, but I’d faint. A big meal with meat would make me sleepy and slow. So about two hours before, I have a small plate of pasta, and a banana, which gives me energy without making me heavy. I also drink a lot of water during the day, but never too much just before I go on, because that would be a disaster. Some of my friends have a special lucky snack, but I don’t believe in luck, only in good habits.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: How do you feel when the curtain goes up?

turns.speaker: d
turns.text: Before that, in the dressing room, I’m shaking, more than I ever was as a child. My hands are cold and my heart is going so fast that I think everybody can hear it. But when the curtain rises, everything goes quiet and I feel calm. Tired comes afterwards, at the end, and bored, never.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What advice would you give to a child who wants to dance?

turns.speaker: d
turns.text: Don’t wait until you’re older, there’s no need, and don’t think about another career yet. Work hard, because nothing comes easy, but make sure you enjoy it. If it’s not fun, it’s very difficult to continue for so many years. I remember that on bad days, when everything hurt, I thought about stopping, and it was the love of dancing that kept me going. A teacher once told me that talent is only ten per cent, and the rest is a happy kind of hard work.
